ability.definition: possession of the means or skill to do something.

access.definition: To connect to a resource, either remotely or locally.
the ability to read from or write to a data store, or the ability to connect to a resource.

accumulator.definition: An expression in an aggregation pipeline that maintains state between documents in the aggregation pipeline. For a list of accumulator operations, see $group.

accumulator operators.definition: Operators in MongoDB that are used in aggregation frameworks to perform calculations on data as it passes through the pipeline.

action.definition: An operation the user can perform on a resource. Actions and resources combine to create privileges. See action.

activity feed.definition: A chronological list of activities or events, often used in social media or project management tools.

admin database.definition: A privileged database. Users must have access to the admin database to run certain administrative commands. For a list of administrative commands, see Administration Commands.

agent.definition: A software component that acts on behalf of a user or another program.

agent API key.definition: A unique identifier that Automation, Monitoring, and Backup Agents for a project use to authenticate themselves to Cloud Manager.

Agg Expressions.definition: Short for Aggregation Expressions, which are used in MongoDB aggregation pipeline stages to perform the data operation.

aggregation.definition: Any of a variety of operations that reduces and summarizes large sets of data. MongoDB's aggregate() and mapReduce() methods are two examples of aggregation operations. For more information, see Aggregation Operations.

aggregation pipeline.definition: The set of MongoDB operators that let you calculate aggregate values without having to use map-reduce. For a list of operators, see Aggregation Reference.

aggregation pipeline stages.definition: The instructions included in a MongoDB aggregation pipeline that specify how documents are transformed, where each stage represents a specific type of transformation.

Agile.definition: A methodology for software development that emphasizes iterative development, collaboration, and flexibility.

alert.definition: Notification sent by Atlas when your database operations or server usage reach thresholds that affect cluster performance. To learn what conditions you can set to trigger alerts, see Review Alert Conditions.

algorithm.definition: A well-defined procedure or set of rules used for performing a task or solving a problem.

analytics.definition: The systematic computational analysis of data or statistics.

analytics node.definition: Specialized read-only node that can isolate queries which you do not want to affect your operational workload. Analytics nodes are useful for handling analytic data such as reporting queries executed by BI tools. You can host analytics nodes in dedicated geographic regions to optimize read performance and reduce latency.

analyze.definition: To examine data methodically for the purpose of explanation and interpretation.

analyzer.definition: A tool or component used to analyze data.

ANN.definition: Approximate Nearest Neighbor; an algorithm or method used to find the closest points in high-dimensional spaces efficiently.

announce.definition: To make a public declaration about a fact, event, or product.

answer.definition: A solution to a problem or response to a question.

application.definition: Software designed to help the user perform specific tasks.

application database.definition: A database used to store and manage data for an application.

translations.es: base de datos de la aplicación

application development.definition: The process of creating software applications.

application ID.definition: A unique identifier for an application.

apply.definition: To use for a purpose or take action on.

arbiter.definition: A member of a replica set that exists solely to vote in elections. Arbiters do not replicate data. See Replica Set Arbiter.

archive.definition: This may refer to data archived by Online Archive, which is a service that moves data you access infrequently to a read-only federated database instance based on rules you configure. In the context of releases, this refers to older releases that are no longer supported.

asset.definition: In the context of leveraging MongoDB to create an Asset Administration Shell, an asset is anything with a unique ID and a mechanism for sending and receiving data.

async.definition: Short for asynchronous, often used in computing to describe operations that occur independently of the main program flow.

atomic operation.definition: An atomic operation is a write operation which either completes entirely, or does not complete at all. In the case of distributed transactions, which involve writes to multiple documents, all writes to each document must succeed for the transaction to succeed. Atomic operations cannot partially complete. See Atomicity and Transactions.

audit.definition: Database auditing lets administrators track system activity for deployments with multiple users. Atlas administrators can select the actions, database users, Atlas roles, and LDAP groups that they want to audit.

authentication.definition: Verification of the user identity. See Authentication.

authentication mechanism.definition: The method used to verify the identity of a user or system. The default authentication mechanism for MongoDB is Salted Challenge Response Authentication Mechanism (SCRAM).

authentication provider.definition: An integration of a specific authentication mechanism intoyour user authentication system.

authentication trigger.definition: Passes an authentication event describing the user and interaction to the linked function.

authorization.definition: Provisioning of access to databases and operations.

Auto-Scale.definition: You can configure the cluster tier ranges that Atlas uses to automatically scale your cluster tier, storage capacity, or both in response to cluster usage.

auto-scaling.definition: Configurable option to have your cluster automatically increase or decrease its cluster tier, storage capacity, or both in response to cluster usage.

automatic encryption.definition: When using In-Use Encryption, automatically performing encryption and decryption based on your preconfigured encryption schema. The Automatic Encryption Shared Library translates MongoDB Query Language into the correct call, meaning you don't need to rewrite your application for specific encrypt and decrypt calls.

automation.definition: The use of technology to perform tasks without human intervention. In the context of MongoDB, this may refer to the assisted management of MongoDB processes through the Ops Manager interface. The MongoDB Agents installed on your MongoDB hosts allow you to deploy, configure, and update MongoDB processes directly from Ops Manager.

Automation Agent.definition: A MongoDB component that manages the automation of certain tasks on every server that ran a mongod or mongos. This has been replaced with the MongoDB Agent.

availability zone.definition: In cloud computing, an "availability zone" refers to an isolated data center within the infrastructure of a cloud service provider. This data center is physically separated from other availability zones and has its own dedicated power, networking, and cooling systems. The concept of Availability Zones is introduced to enhance the reliability and fault tolerance of systems.

B-tree.definition: A data structure commonly used by database management systems to store indexes. MongoDB uses B-trees for its indexes.

backend.definition: The part of a software system that handles business logic, database interactions, and server-side operations.

background.definition: Running a process without user interaction, typically in the background of a system or application.

backing databases.definition: The collective term for the sets of MongoDB databases that support an Ops Manager deployment: the application database and the backup database(s).

backlink.definition: A backlink is a link within a RealmObject that indicates that the RealmObject has an inverse relationship with another RealmObject. An embedded object should have a backlink to its parent object.

backup.definition: Copy of your data that encapsulates the state of your cluster at a given time. Backups provide a safety measure in the case of data loss events.

Backup Agent.definition: A component that ran within your data center and backed up MongoDB processes via the MongoDB wire protocol. This has been replaced with the MongoDB Agent.

backup blockstore database.definition: The blockstore database stores a snapshot in a storage format that parses the snapshot into smaller chunks that allow Ops Manager to manage snapshot changes.

translations.es: base de datos de almacenamiento en bloques de copias de seguridad

backup cursor.definition: A tailable cursor that points to a list of backup files. Backup cursors are for internal use only.

Backup Daemon.definition: The Ops Manager component that creates and manages backups by maintaining head databases and snapshots for FCV 4.0 and earlier. Starting with FCV 4.2, onprem uses backup cursors instead of head databases.

Backup Database.definition: A secondary database used to ensure data can be restored in case of corruption or loss of the primary database.

translations.es: base de datos de copias de seguridad

backup job.definition: A scheduled task that performs the operation of backing up data from the primary database to a backup storage.

balancer.definition: An internal MongoDB process that runs in the context of a sharded cluster and manages the migration of chunks. Administrators must disable the balancer for all maintenance operations on a sharded cluster.

batch.definition: To process a series of commands or tasks as a single unit, often to improve efficiency or performance.

best practices.definition: Established industry standards and guidelines that are recommended for achieving optimal outcomes.

block.definition: a chunk or section of a larger whole
The behavior where a program waits for a network operation to complete before proceeding

blocking sort.definition: A sort that must be performed in memory before output is returned. Blocking sorts may impact performance for large data sets. Use an indexed sort to avoid a blocking sort.

blockstore.definition: A storage format in MongoDB backups that organizes snapshots into smaller chunks for efficient management.

blog.definition: online journal where an individual, group, or corporation presents a record of activities, thoughts, or beliefs
To write entries or posts for a website or platform dedicated to the publishing of online articles or blogs.

blog post.definition: A single article or entry on a blog, typically discussing a specific topic.

blog series.definition: A collection of related blog posts that explore a topic in depth over multiple entries.

boolean.definition: A data type with two possible values: true or false, used in logical operations.

bounded collection scan.definition: A plan used by the query optimizer that eliminates documents with specific field value ranges. For example, if a range of date field values is outside of a specified date range, the documents in that range are eliminated from the query plan.

breaking change.definition: A modification in software development that causes previously functioning features or dependencies to fail.

build.definition: To compile source code into executable programs or applications.

builders.definition: Developers or engineers who create, construct, or maintain systems, applications, or features.

built-in.definition: A feature or functionality that is included as part of the standard software package.

cache.definition: A storage layer that temporarily holds data to speed up subsequent data retrieval requests.

call.definition: An instruction or statement that transfers program execution to some section of code, such as a subroutine, to perform a specific task

callback.definition: A function passed as an argument to another function, which is then invoked after the completion of the higher-order function.

canonical mode.definition: A specific state or configuration that serves as the standardized or recognized form.

capability.definition: The ability or features that a system, software, or application possesses to perform functions.

capacity.definition: The maximum amount of data that a system or storage can handle or contain.

capped collection.definition: A fixed-sized collection that automatically overwrites its oldest entries when it reaches its maximum size. The MongoDB oplog that is used in replication is a capped collection.

cardinality.definition: The measure of the number of elements within a set of values. For example, the set A = { 2, 4, 6 } contains 3 elements, and has a cardinality of 3.

cartesian product.definition: The result of combining two data sets such that the combined set contains every possible combination of values.

Causal Consistency.definition: A consistency model for distributed systems ensuring that operations are observed in the same order in which they were issued.

certificate stores.definition: Repositories used to store and manage digital certificates for authentication.

cfq.definition: Complete Fairness Queueing (cfq) is a I/O operation scheduler that allocates bandwidth for incoming request processes.

translations.es: CFQ (Planificador de I/O de Equidad Completa)

challenge.definition: A task or problem that tests a person's abilities or the capabilities of a system.

channel.definition: A medium for communication or data transfer within or between systems.

checkpoint.definition: A saved state of a database or system at a specific point in time.

checksum.definition: A calculated value used to ensure data integrity. The md5 algorithm is sometimes used as a checksum.

chunk.definition: A contiguous range of shard key values within a particular shard. Chunk ranges are inclusive of the lower boundary and exclusive of the upper boundary. MongoDB splits chunks when they grow beyond the configured chunk size, which by default is 128 megabytes. MongoDB migrates chunks when a shard contains too many chunks of a collection relative to other shards.

class.definition: In MongoDB, a class is used to represent data in a collection.

client.definition: The application layer that uses a database for data persistence and storage. Drivers provide the interface level between the application layer and the database server.  Client can also refer to a single thread or process.

client affinity.definition: A consistent client connection to a specified data source.

client database.definition: A database used to store client-specific information or accessed directly by client applications.

client reset.definition: client reset is a Device Sync error that signals an Atlas Device SDK client database cannot sync data with the App Services App

client-side.definition: Operations or processing that occur on the client's machine rather than on the server.

cloud.definition: A location on the internet where data and applications are stored and accessed.

cloud backups.definition: Localized cluster backup storage using the native snapshot functionality of the cluster's cloud service provider.

translations.es: copias de seguridad en la nube

Cloud Migration.definition: The process of moving data, applications, and services from on-premises infrastructure to a cloud computing environment.

cloud provider.definition: A company that offers cloud computing services.

cluster.definition: Set of nodes comprising a MongoDB deployment. In Atlas, clusters can be replica sets or sharded deployments.

cluster class.definition: Configurable for M40+ clusters hosted on AWS. Storage class of your cluster. Your selected class affects cluster storage performance and cluster costs.

cluster tier.definition: Dictates the memory, storage, vCPUs, and IOPS specification for each data-bearing server in the cluster. Cluster storage size and overall performance increase as the cluster tier increases.

clustered collection.definition: A collection that stores documents ordered by a clustered index key.

collation.definition: The rules that define the sorting and comparing of data.

collection.definition: A grouping of MongoDB documents. A collection is the equivalent of an RDBMS table. A collection exists within a single database. Collections do not enforce a schema. Documents within a collection can have different fields. Typically, all documents in a collection have a similar or related purpose.

collection scan.definition: Collection scans are a query execution strategy where MongoDB must inspect every document in a collection to see if it matches the query criteria. These queries are very inefficient and do not use indexes.

collection statistics.definition: Metrics that provide information about the performance and status of a database collection.

command line.definition: A text-based user interface for interacting with comptuer programs. Synonymous with command line interface.

command line interface.definition: A means of interacting with a computer program through text-based commands.

commit.definition: the act of making of a set of tentative changes permanent, marking the end of a transaction

commit quorum.definition: During an index build the commit quorum specifies how many secondaries must be ready to commit their local index build before the primary node will execute the commit.

compaction.definition: Allocation and deallocation of data within a Realm Database and/or exceeding the size of physical memory can lead to fragmentation on disk. Calling the compact method reorganizes internal data structures to reduce the storage overhead of local realms in the event of fragmentation.

company.definition: A business organization that sells goods or services.

compliance.definition: Conforming to rules, standards, or laws.

compound hashed shard keys.definition: Shard keys in MongoDB that combine hashed and non-hashed fields to distribute data across shards.

translations.es: claves de partición compuestas con hash

compound index.definition: An index consisting of two or more keys.

compound operator.definition: A database opertator that combines two or more clauses into a single query statement.

compression.definition: Reducing the size of data to save space or transmission time.

concurrency control.definition: Concurrency control ensures that database operations can be executed concurrently without compromising correctness. Pessimistic concurrency control, such as used in systems with locks, will block any potentially conflicting operations even if they may not turn out to actually conflict. Optimistic concurrency control, the approach used by WiredTiger, will delay checking until after a conflict may have occurred, aborting and retrying one of the operations involved in any write conflict that arises.

conf call.definition: Abbreviation of conference call, an audio and/or video call in which multiple participants are connected.

config database.definition: An internal database that holds the metadata associated with a sharded cluster. Applications and administrators should not modify the config database in the course of normal operation.

config server.definition: A mongod instance that stores all the metadata associated with a sharded cluster.

configuration file.definition: A file containing settings and options for software or hardware.

conflict resolution.definition: strategies that determine which change to apply when two or more users make changes to the same piece of data independently

connection pool.definition: A cache of database connections maintained by the driver. These connections are re-used when connections to the database are required, instead of opening new connections.

connection pooling.definition: Managing two or more connections that can be reused for multiple requests, improving performance and resource utilization.

connection string.definition: A text string that specifies the information needed to establish a connection with a database.

consistency.definition: Ensuring that data remains accurate and consistent across a system.

consistent.definition: Always behaving or performing in a similar way.

consulting.definition: The practice of providing expert advice in a particular area.

contact.definition: Information used to communicate with a person or organization.

container.definition: A collected set of software and its dependent libraries that are packaged together to make transferring between computing environments easier. Containers run as compartmentalized processes on your operating system, and can be given their own resource constraints. Common container technologies are Docker and Kubernetes.

Convenient Transaction API.definition: A MongoDB framework that allows users to perform transactions without having to manually commit or end them.

copy-on-write.definition: A resource-management technique used in computer programming to efficiently implement a "duplicate" or "copy" operation on modifiable resources

cost.definition: The amount required to purchase or maintain something.

coverage.definition: The extent to which something is covered or addressed.

crate.definition: A crate is a compilation unit in Rust.

credentials.definition: a set of authentication information used to establish secure connections and access control. Credentials are used to verify the identity of clients, applications and users.

credit.definition: The trust that allows one party to provide money or resources to another party without requiring immediate reimbursement.

cursor.definition: A pointer to the result set of a query. Clients can iterate through a cursor to retrieve results. By default, cursors not opened within a session automatically timeout after 10 minutes of inactivity. Cursors opened under a session close with the end or timeout of the session.

Custom Aggregation Expressions.definition: User-defined expressions used in MongoDB's aggregation framework to perform custom data transformations or analysis.

custom analyzer.definition: A user-defined tool that analyzes data, allowing you to modify or better understand its contents.

custom role.definition: Custom set of MongoDB privilege actions and MongoDB roles that you can save and assign to database users. Create custom roles when Atlas's built-in roles don't describe your desired set of privileges.

custom snapshot.definition: A user-defined snapshot of a database at a specific point in time.

custom user data.definition: Developers can define data that they want to associate with a specific user, such as birthday, favorite color, operating system or other details

custom user data cluster.definition: MongoDB Atlas cluster which has a database that has a collection that stores arbitrary custom information about a user

translations.es: clúster de datos de usuario personalizado

custom user data collection.definition: MongoDB collection which stores arbitrary custom information about a user

translations.es: colección de datos de usuario personalizada

custom user data database.definition: MongoDB database which has a collection that stores arbitrary custom information about a user

translations.es: base de datos de usuario personalizada

customer.definition: An individual or organization that purchases goods or services.

customer master key.definition: A key that is used to encrypt your Data Encryption Key. The customer master key should be hosted in a remote key provider.

Customer Support.definition: Assistance provided by a company to its customers to help them use products or services effectively.

daemon.definition: The conventional name for a background, non-interactive process.

dashboard.definition: A user interface that provides visualizations and summaries of information for monitoring and analysis.

data access.definition: The ability to retrieve or manipulate data.

data at rest.definition: Data that is stored on a physical medium and not being transmitted.

data directory.definition: The file-system location where the mongod stores data files. The dbPath option specifies the data directory.

Data Encryption Key.definition: A key you use to encrypt the fields in your MongoDB documents. The encrypted Data Encryption Key is stored in your Key Vault collection. The Data Encryption Key is encrypted by the Customer Master Key.

data file.definition: A file that contains data, typically in a structured format.

data management.definition: The practice of handling an organization's data so it can be analyzed for decision making.

data model.definition: The organization of data within a database and the links between related entities.

data partition.definition: A distributed system architecture that splits data into ranges. Sharding uses partitioning.

data source.definition: A MongoDB Atlas cluster or Data Lake that is associated with your App.

data transfer.definition: The process of moving data from one location to another.

data type.definition: An attribute of a variable that determines what kind of values it can hold.

data-center awareness.definition: A property that allows clients to address members in a system based on their locations. Replica sets implement data-center awareness using tagging.

database.definition: A physical container for collections. Each database gets its own set of files on the file system. A single MongoDB server typically has multiple databases.

database command.definition: A MongoDB operation, other than an insert, update, remove, or query.

database deployment.definition: The process of setting up and configuring MongoDB instances to create a working database environment.

translations.es: implementación de la base de datos

database profiler.definition: A tool that, when enabled, keeps a record on all long-running operations in a database's system.profile collection. The profiler is most often used to diagnose slow queries.

database trigger.definition: Passes a change event describing the data that changed to the linked function.

database user.definition: Credentials used to authenticate a client to access a MongoDB database deployment. You can assign privileges to a database user to determine that user's access level to a database deployment. Database users are different from Atlas users. Database users have access to MongoDB deployments, not the Atlas application.

database user privileges.definition: Set of privilege actions or roles granted to a database user. You can assign database user privileges at the database deployment, database, and collection level.

translations.es: privilegios de usuario de base de datos

dead letter queue.definition: A dead letter queue is a collection within an Atlas database that stores documents that throw errors during ingestion.

dedicated cluster.definition: Cluster category containing clusters of tier M10 and greater.

deduplication.definition: The process of eliminating duplicate copies of data.

default.definition: The preset option selected automatically unless a user specifies otherwise.

delayed member.definition: A replica set member that cannot become primary and applies operations at a specified delay. The delay is useful for protecting data from human error (i.e. unintentionally deleted databases) or updates that have unforeseen effects on the production database.

delayed members.definition: Members of a MongoDB replica set that replicate data with a delay to maintain a historical copy of the data, which allows for data recovery.

dense index.definition: An index that contains an entry for every possible search key.

deploy.definition: The process of making an application or system available for use.

deployment.definition: A group of MongoDB servers containing your data. Atlas-managed database deployments are either clusters (replica sets or sharded clusters) or serverless instances.

description.definition: A detailed explanation or portrayal of various attributes, functionality, and properties of an item or concept.

developer.definition: A person who writes and maintains software code.

development mode.definition: A toggle that, when enabled, automatically updates your Realm Schema to match the Realm Object Model used by synced client applications.

director.definition: A person in charge of a specific area within an organization.

directory.definition: A file system structure used to organize files or folders.

dirty bytes.definition: Data that has been modified in memory but has not yet been written to the disk.

disaster recovery.definition: process of restoring critical systems and data after a disruptive event to ensure business continuity.

distinguished name.definition: A name that uniquely identifies an entry in a directory, e.g. an LDAP directory.

distributed transactions.definition: Transactions that involve two or more network hosts and maintain data integrity for updates across multiple databases and systems.

document.definition: A record in a MongoDB collection and the basic unit of data in MongoDB. Documents are analogous to JSON objects but exist in the database in a more type-rich format known as BSON.

dot notation.definition: MongoDB uses the dot notation to access the elements of an array and to access the fields of an embedded document.

download.definition: The process of receiving data from a remote system to a local system.

downloads.definition: Data that has been loaded to a local system.

draining.definition: The process of removing or "shedding" chunks from one shard to another. Administrators must drain shards before removing them from the cluster.

driver.definition: These are pieces of software that we produce.   A client library for interacting with MongoDB in a particular language.  They're essentially translation layers, letting you interact with MongoDB directly in various programming languages: so you have the Python driver, the C driver, and so on.

driver releases.definition: Updates and new versions of database drivers, which allow applications to interact with MongoDB.

drop.definition: To remove an association or connection

durable.definition: A write operation is durable when it will persist across a shutdown (or crash) and restart of one or more server processes. For a single mongod server, a write operation is considered durable when it has been written to the server's journal file. For a replica set, a write operation is considered durable once the write operation is durable on a majority of voting nodes; i.e. written to a majority of voting nodes' journals.

efficiency.definition: The ability to accomplish a task with minimal waste of time and resources.

electable node.definition: Node which is eligible to become the primary member of your replica set. Atlas prioritizes nodes in the Highest Priority region for primary eligibility during elections. To ensure reliable elections, the total number of electable nodes across an entire region must be 3, 5, or 7.

election.definition: The process by which members of a replica set select a primary on startup and in the event of a failure.

embedded document.definition: A document stored within another document in a nested structure in document-based databases like MongoDB.

embedded expression.definition: You can embed multiple expression documents in the fields of another expression document to handle complex evaluation logic.

embedded object.definition: object that is nested within a parent object and never exists independent of the parent object

embedding.definition: A vector (numerical array) representation of data capturing its semantic meaning

enable.definition: to turn on an option or functionality, activate
to empower or give someone the ability to do something, use

encrypted.definition: The process of securing data by converting it into a code to prevent unauthorized access.

encryption.definition: The method by which plaintext is converted into ciphertext to protect data from unauthorized access.

encryption at rest.definition: Encryption of data when it is stored on a physical medium. This is in contrast to data being transferred.

encryption key.definition: Random string of bits generated specifically to encrypt and decrypt data.  Atlas Project Owners can configure an additional layer of encryption on their data in addition to the default encryption at rest that Atlas provides. Project owners can use their Atlas-compatible customer key management provider with the MongoDB encrypted storage engine.

enforce.definition: to give force to : strengthen, to urge with energy enforce arguments

engagement.definition: Interaction between a company and its customers or users.

engine.definition: The storage engine is the component of the database that is responsible for managing how data is stored.

enterprise.definition: A large organization or company, especially in the context of business applications and services. At MongoDB, this may refer to the MongoDB Enterprise product.

enterprise authentication.definition: Authentication mechanisms designed for enterprise-level applications, often integrating with existing enterprise identity systems. This may specifically refer to authentication methods when using the MongoDB Enterprise product.

enterprise security.definition: Comprehensive security measures implemented to protect an enterprise's information systems. This may specifically refer to security features within the MongoDB Enterprise product.

envelope encryption.definition: An encryption practice where data is encrypted using a Data Encryption Key and the data encryption key is encrypted by another key called the Customer Master Key. Encrypted keys are stored within a MongoDB collection referred to as the KeyVault as BSON documents.

equality match.definition: A comparison operation in databases where the values must match exactly.

event.definition: An occurrence or happening, often used in the context of user actions or system operations. MongoDB products contain many mechanisms to track and report on specific types of events.

event loop.definition: A design pattern in which a central loop waits for signals from a UI or other source before updating underlying data structures.

eventual consistency.definition: A property of a distributed system that allows changes to the system to propagate gradually. In a database system, this means that readable members are not required to reflect the latest writes at all times.

example.definition: A specific case or instance used to illustrate a concept.

excluded namespace.definition: A namespace in a database that is excluded from certain operations, like backup or indexing.

exclusive lock.definition: A type of locking mechanisum used in computer suystems and databases to ensure that only one process or thread can have exclusive access to a resource or a piece of data at a time

expansion.definition: a variable that represents a dynamic value in an expression

expertise.definition: Specialized skill or knowledge in a particular field.

explicit encryption.definition: When using In-Use Encryption, explicitly specifying the encryption or decryption operation, keyID, and query type (for Queryable Encryption) or algorithm (for Client-Side Field Level Encryption) when working with encrypted data.

expression.definition: a JSON object that controls data access with conditional permissions; In the context of an aggregation pipeline, expressions are the stateless transformations that operate on the data that passes through a pipeline.

external dependencies.definition: One or more JavaScript modules from npm that you have uploaded to your App.

extra.definition: Additional or more than what is usual.

facet.definition: An element or component used to categorize or filter data, often used in search engines. When performing a query, a facet is an operator that groups results by values or ranges in the specified faceted fields.

feature.definition: specifications of a particular product. Note that this usage is different from "featured event" as it is used above below.

feature compatibility version.definition: The version of a database feature that ensures compatibility between different database versions. You can upgrade or downgrade MongoDB versions within the same Feature Compatibility Version, sometimes abbreviated as FCV.

federated.definition: Association of multiple systems or services to act together, often seen in identity management or databases.

federated database instance.definition: federated in this context refers to ways to combine multiple databases

translations.es: instancia federada de base de datos

federated queries.definition: Queries that access and merge data from multiple sources or databases.

field.definition: A name-value pair in a document. A document has zero or more fields. Fields are analogous to columns in relational databases.

field level encryption.definition: Encrypting individual fields within a document in a database.

field path.definition: Path to a field in the document. To specify a field path, use a string that prefixes the field name with a dollar sign ($).

file.definition: A digital document or piece of data stored on a computer system.

filter.definition: This term refers to a quuery specification used to retrieve specfic documents from a collection

Financial Services.definition: This term describes a specific industry.

find multiple.definition: an operation that returns more than one result from a collection based on a query that you provide.

find multiple documents.definition: an operation that returns more than one document from a MongoDB namespace (database.collection) based on a query that you provide.

find one.definition: an operation that returns one result from a collection based on a query that you provide.

find one document.definition: an operation that returns one document from a MongoDB namespace (database.collection) based on a query that you provide.

flexible data.definition: A characteristic of MongoDB data that enables documents in a collection to have different sets of fields and field data types to differ between documents.

format.definition: The structure or layout of data.

free tier.definition: Free-to-use cluster tier that provides a small-scale development environment to host your data. free clusters never expire, and provide access to a subset of Atlas features and functionality. free clusters might also be referred to by their instance size, M0.

Full Text Search indexes.definition: an index on a property that enables Full Text Search queries

fully-managed.definition: "fully managed" is a feature of our product.

function context.definition: Atlas Functions have access to a global context object that contains metadata for the incoming requests and provides access to components and services that you've configured in your App Services App

function executions.definition: when a user calls a function from a client app or when a function calls an external service

generative AI.definition: A type of artificial intelligence that can generate new content, such as text, images, or music.

GeoJSON point.definition: A data type representing a single location that you can store in GeoJSON, a format for geospatial data.

global cluster.definition: Clusters with defined geographic zones to support location-aware read and write operations for globally distributed application instances and clients. You can enable global sharding on clusters of tier M30 and greater.

global write zone.definition: Geographic zone representing a subset of your global cluster distribution. Each Global Cluster supports up to 9 distinct global write zones. Each zone consists of one Highest Priority region and one or more electable, read-only, or analytics regions.  The available geographic regions depend on the selected cloud service provider.

government.definition: A governing body of a nation, state, or community.

graph.definition: Note that this is not graph as in "a visual representation of data", like a chart. This is a computer science concept of graph, which is more like "network" (e.g., a "social graph").

GraphQL requests.definition: when a client application issues a GraphQL query operation or calls a custom resolver

GridFS.definition: A convention for storing large files in a MongoDB database. All of the official MongoDB drivers support this convention, as does the mongofiles program.

groom.definition: An Ops Manager job type that removes unused blocks on a blockstore and moves blocks from one blockstore to another.

group.definition: The operation used to aggregate data based on a specified criteria
Logical grouping of database deployments. You can have multiple database deployments within a single project and multiple projects within a single organization.

group ID.definition: the project's unique Project ID value, sometimes referred to as a "Group ID", used to identify and work with your App Services App programatically

guarantees.definition: Assurances that certain conditions will be fulfilled.

guide.definition: A document or person that provides information and instructions.

handle.definition: In this context, "respond to," "deal with," or "manage" would all be fine

hardware.definition: Physical components of a computer system.

hashed.definition: Data that has been transformed using a hash function to protect its integrity.

hashed shard key.definition: A special type of shard key that uses a hash of the value in the shard key field to distribute documents among members of the sharded cluster.

head database.definition: The copy of a backed-up deployment stored on the Backup Daemon's server. The daemon maintains a head database for each shard or replica set it backs up and creates periodic snapshots. The Daemon stores the head databases in the head directory.

head directory.definition: The dedicated disk partition on the Backup Daemon's host where the Backup Daemon stores the head databases. The daemon writes to this directory as the mongodb-mms user.

health check.definition: A process for assessing the status or health of an application or system.

health manager.definition: A health manager runs health checks on a health manager facet at a specified intensity level. Health manager checks run at specified time intervals. A health manager can be configured to move a failing mongos out of a cluster automatically.

health manager facet.definition: A specific set of features and functionality that a health manager can be configured to run health checks against. For example, you can configure a health manager to monitor and manage DNS or LDAP cluster health issues automatically.

translations.es: faceta de gestión de verificaciónes de estado

hedged read.definition: A deprecated MongoDB read operation that sends the same request to multiple replicas to reduce latency.

helper.definition: A function or tool that assists with tasks.

hexadecimal string.definition: A hexadecimal string is a representation of data using base-16 numbering, consisting of digits 0-9 and letters A-F.

hidden member.definition: A replica set member that cannot become primary and are invisible to client applications.

high availability.definition: High availability indicates a system designed for durability, redundancy, and automatic failover such that the applications supported by the system can operate continuously and without downtime for a long period of time.

highest priority region.definition: Region in a multi-region cluster which Atlas prioritizes for primary eligibility during elections.

host.definition: usage here is not "host" as in a person who receives or entertains guests, but as a web hosting service.

hot shards.definition: In sharding, shards that receive a disproportionately high number of requests, causing potential performance issues.

human-readable label.definition: A text label that is easily understood by humans, often used for identifying data fields or records.

idempotent.definition: The quality of an operation to produce the same result given the same input, whether run once or run multiple times.

identity provider.definition: An identity provider (abbreviated IdP or IDP) is a system entity that creates, maintains, and manages identity information for principals and also provides authentication services to relying applications within a federation or distributed network

idiomatic.definition: Using figurative expressions that are natural to native speakers of a language.

impact.definition: Region in a multi-region cluster which Atlas prioritizes for primary eligibility during elections.

implement.definition: To put a plan or system into operation.

implementation.definition: The process of putting a plan or system into effect.

IMPORTANT.definition: Signifying something of high priority or urgency.

In-Use Encryption.definition: Encryption that secures data while being transmitted, stored, and processed, and enables supported queries on that encrypted data.

index.definition: A data structure that optimizes queries. Indexes are special data structures that store a small portion of data in order to support the efficient execution of queries.

index bounds.definition: The range of index values that MongoDB searches when using an index to fulfill a query.

index build.definition: an index build refers to the process of creating a data structure that improves query performance by allowing faster retrieval of documents based on specific fields.

index entry.definition: An index entry refers to a specific element within an index

indexed document.definition: A document that has been stored in a way that makes it easy to quickly locate and retrieve specific data.

indexed sort.definition: A sort in which an index provides the sorted result. Sort operations that use an index often have better performance than a blocking sort.

indexing.definition: Indexes are special data structures that store a small portion of data in order to support the efficient execution of queries.

inequality operator.definition: An inequality operator is a comparison operator that checks whether two values are not equal.

init script.definition: A simple shell script used by a Linux platform's init system to start, restart, or stop a daemon process. If you installed MongoDB via a package manager, an init script has been provided for your system as part of the installation.

init system.definition: The init system is the first process started on a Linux platform after the kernel starts, and manages all other processes on the system. The init system uses an init script to start, restart, or stop a daemon process, such as mongod or mongos. Recent versions of Linux tend to use the systemd init system, which uses the systemctl command, while older versions tend to use the System V init system, which uses the service command.

initial sync.definition: The replica set operation that replicates data from an existing replica set member to a new replica set member.

insight.definition: An understanding or perception of something.

instance.definition: An instance is simply a case or occurrence of something.

intent lock.definition: A lock on a resource that indicates that the holder of the lock will read (intent shared) or write (intent exclusive) the resource using concurrency control at a finer granularity than that of the resource with the intent lock. Intent locks allow concurrent readers and writers of a resource.

interact.definition: To communicate or make contact with someone or something.

interface endpoint.definition: Elastic network interface with a private IP address from the IP address range of your VPC subnet on AWS. An interface endpoint serves as an entry point for traffic from clients in your VPC to an Atlas cluster when you create a AWS PrivateLink connection between an AWS VPC and Atlas clusters in a specified region.

interrupt point.definition: A point in an operation's lifecycle when it can safely abort. MongoDB only terminates an operation at designated interrupt points.

IP access list.definition: List of IP addresses and CIDR blocks with access to clusters within an Atlas project. Atlas only allows client connections to a cluster from entries in the corresponding project's IP access list. The access list can have up to 200 entries.

IPv6.definition: acronym: internet protocol version 6; A revision to the IP (Internet Protocol) standard that provides a significantly larger address space to more effectively support the number of hosts on the contemporary Internet.

ISODate.definition: The international date format used by mongosh to display dates. The format is: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM.SS.millis.

isolation.definition: "Isolation" is a property or trait of a database transaction which ensures that each transation is kept separate. It is the "I" in the ACID abbreviation.

job.definition: A scheduled task or process, often in the context of computing or database operations.

journal.definition: A sequential, binary transaction log used to bring the database into a valid state in the event of a hard shutdown. Journaling writes data first to the journal and then to the core data files. MongoDB enables journaling by default for 64-bit builds of MongoDB version 2.0 and newer. Journal files are pre-allocated and exist as files in the data directory.

journaling.definition: Journaling writes data first to the journal and then to the core data files.

jumbo chunk.definition: A chunk in a MongoDB sharded cluster that grows beyond the specified chunk size but cannot be split, often causing performance bottlenecks.

JVM.definition: Java Virtual Machine, a virtual machine that enables a computer to run Java programs.

key material.definition: The random string of bits used by an encryption algorithm to encrypt and decrypt data.

Key Vault Collection.definition: A MongoDB collection used to store the encrypted Data Encryption Keys as BSON documents.

Knowledge Base.definition: a store of information or data

kubernetes secret.definition: A Kubernetes secret is an object that contains a small amount of sensitive data such as a password, a token, or a key.

language.definition: When used in a programming context, a system of notation for writing computer programs that usually includes a type system, variables, and mechanisms for error handling.

large language model.definition: A type of AI model trained on a vast amount of text data to understand and generate human language.

latest release.definition: The most recent version of a software product or service.

LDAP authorization.definition: The process of determining what an authenticated user is permitted to do within a system or application. This involves assigning permissions and access rights to users based on their identity, which has already been verified through the LDAP authentication process. The directory services provided by LDAP, such as Active Directory or OpenLDAP, contain information about users, groups, and other objects, and the access control policies are enforced based on this directory information.

learn.definition: To acquire knowledge or skill through study or experience.

least privilege.definition: An authorization policy that gives a user only the amount of access that is essential to that user's work and no more.

legacy.definition: Older version of software or systems that are no longer the current release, but are still supported or in use

legacy backups.definition: Incremental backups of your cluster taken by Atlas that ensure that your backups are typically just a few seconds behind the operational system. You can restore your cluster to a state from a selected point in time within the last 24 hours.

library.definition: a collection of programs and software packages made generally available

linearizable.definition: A property of a system where operations appear to occur instantaneously in some order.

LineString.definition: A LineString is defined by an array of two or more positions.

link-token.definition: String that contains the information necessary to connect from Cloud Manager or Ops Manager to Atlas during a live migration from a Cloud Manager or Ops Manager deployment to a cluster in Atlas.  When you are ready to live migrate data from a Cloud Manager or Ops Manager deployment, you generate a link-token in Atlas and then enter it in your Cloud Manager or Ops Manager organization's settings. You use the same link-token to migrate each deployment in your Cloud Manager or Ops Manager organization sequentially, one at a time. You can generate multiple link-tokens in Atlas. Use one unique link-token for each Cloud Manager or Ops Manager organization.

linked cluster.definition: A MongoDB Atlas database cluster that is associated with your App.

Live Migration.definition: Process to seamlessly move an existing source replica set or sharded cluster to Atlas. During the live migration process, Atlas keeps the target cluster in sync with the remote source until you cut your applications over to the Atlas cluster.

live objects.definition: Atlas Device SDK objects are direct proxies to the underlying stored data and automatically update whenever they're modified

locale.definition: Set of parameters that defines a user's language and/or country. For example: hu, en-GB.

lock.definition: MongoDB uses locks to ensure that concurrency does not affect correctness. MongoDB uses read locks, write locks and intent locks.

log.definition: Term of art for a record of things that happened in some system (MongoDB or other), sort of like a log book. You'll encounter "log", "logging", "log data", and so on. Check whether the target language translates – good chance it doesn't.

log file.definition: A file maintained by MongoDB that stores a running log of events, including incoming connections, commands run, and issues encountered.

log in.definition: The process of gaining access to a computer system or application.

log out.definition: The action of ending a session or connection by a user, typically on a computer system, website or application

LVM.definition: Logical volume manager. LVM is a program that abstracts disk images from physical devices and provides a number of raw disk manipulation and snapshot capabilities useful for system management.

machine learning.definition: A field of artificial intelligence that uses statistical techniques to give computers the ability to learn from data.

maintenance window.definition: Day and time of the week when Atlas should start weekly maintenance on your cluster. You can set your maintenance window in your Project Settings.

majority.definition: To control or direct the use of resources.

manage.definition: Operated and maintained by a third party.

managed.definition: A database that is hosted in the cloud and operated and maintained by a third party.

managed cloud database.definition: The process of controlling or directing the use of resources.

translations.es: base de tados gestionada en la nube

management.definition: A software solution that enables the administration and control of applications, data, and IT services.

manager.definition: The promotion and selling of products or services, including market research and advertising.

map-reduce.definition: A data processing and aggregation paradigm consisting of a "map" phase that selects data and a "reduce" phase that transforms the data. In MongoDB, you can run arbitrary aggregations over data using map-reduce.

mapping type.definition: A Structure in programming languages that associate keys with values, where keys may nest other pairs of keys and values (e.g. dictionaries, hashes, maps, and associative arrays). The properties of these structures depend on the language specification and implementation. Generally the order of keys in mapping types is arbitrary and not guaranteed.

marketing.definition: Pre-computed aggregation pipeline results that are stored on and read from disk.

materialized views.definition: In the context of files and file types, media refers to multimedia file types such as images, audio, video etc.

md5.definition: A hashing algorithm used to efficiently provide reproducible unique strings to identify and checksum data. MongoDB uses md5 to identify chunks of data for GridFS.

media.definition: A stack of technologies for building web applications, consisting of MongoDB, Express.js, React, and Node.js.

median.definition: In a dataset, the median is the percentile value where 50% of the data falls at or below that value.

member selection.definition: Data that provides information about other data. For example, a MongoDB cluster's metadata contains a mapping of all chunks and shards in the cluster.

metadata.definition: A multinational technology company known for its software products, including the Windows operating system and Office suite.

metadata collection.definition: In Queryable Encryption, the internal collections MongoDB uses to enable querying on encrypted fields.

metrics.definition: Microsoft's cloud computing platform and services.

migrate.definition: A server that is running a dedicated MongoDB Agent automating live migration operations.

migration.definition: The shortest possible period during which a service is unavailable.

migration host.definition: A read operation in a MongoDB replica set that can be served by any replica, reducing latency and balancing load.

MIME.definition: Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions. A standard set of type and encoding definitions used to declare the encoding and type of data in multiple data storage, transmission, and email contexts. The mongofiles tool provides an option to specify a MIME type to describe a file inserted into GridFS storage.

minimal downtime.definition: A software application designed to run on a mobile device, such as a smartphone or tablet.

mirrored reads.definition: Updating or transforming systems, applications, or infrastructure to current standards and technologies.

mobile app.definition: A MongoDB service that synchronizes data between a MongoDB Atlas cluster and client devices in real-time.

mode.definition: The mode is the most common number that appears in a data set.

modernization.definition: Object Data Modeling (ODM) library for MongoDB and Node.js, providing a schema-based solution to model application data.

modulo operation.definition: The modulo operation finds the remainder after division of one number by another.

monitor.definition: A MongoDB component that collects and sends monitoring data to a central location.

monitoring.definition: A property where a sequence only increases or remains constant, never decreases.

monitoring agent.definition: A sequence of operations performed across multiple documents that are committed together, ensuring ACID properties.

monotonic.definition: Shard keys whose values can be changed after the initial assignment.

multi-cloud.definition: The use of cloud services from more than one cloud vendor

multi-document transaction.definition: An open-source relational database management system (RDBMS).

multi-region cluster.definition: Atlas cluster spanning multiple geographic regions. Multi-region clusters can increase availability and improve performance by routing application queries to the most appropriate geographic regions.

namespace.definition: The canonical name for a collection or index in MongoDB. The namespace is a combination of the database name and the name of the collection or index, like so: [database-name].[collection-or-index-name]. All documents belong to a namespace.

native.definition: "native" here means a product feature that is built specificly for that platform.

natural order.definition: The order in which the database refers to documents on disk. This is the default sort order.

network partition.definition: A network failure that separates a distributed system into partitions such that nodes in one partition cannot communicate with the nodes in the other partition.

network peering connection.definition: Process by which two Internet networks connect and exchange traffic. You can directly peer your VPC with the Atlas VPC created for your MongoDB clusters. Using network peering, your application servers can directly connect to Atlas while remaining isolated from public networks.

next.definition: coming immediately after the present one in order, rank, or space

node.definition: An individual mongod process. A replica set has multiple nodes. A node is also known as a member.

non-breaking change.definition: A change that does not interrupt or disrupt existing functionality.

non-relational.definition: A database that does not use the traditional table-based schema of rows and columns.

notifications.definition: In Atlas Device SDK, you can listen for changes to the underlying data referenced by objects - these updates are called notifications

null partition.definition: A null partition is the default realm on the client device.

NVMe storage.definition: For applications hosted on AWS which require low-latency and high-throughput IO, you can use the NVMe cluster class. The NVMe cluster class leverages a unique data protocol to greatly improve data access speeds.  NVMe clusters use a hidden secondary node consisting of a provisioned volume with high throughput and IOPS to facilitate backup.

object.definition: an abstract data type with the addition of polymorphism and inheritance. Rather than structure programs as code and data, an object-oriented system integrates the two using the concept of an "object". An object has state (data) and behavior (code).

object model.definition: the Atlas Device SDK object model is a collection of properties and their types that define how to store and retrieve the object's data

object schema.definition: an object schema is a configuration object that defines the properties and relationships of an Atlas Device SDK object

offload.definition: To transfer or outsource tasks or processes to another system or service as a way to reduce load and improve performance.

on-demand.definition: Services or resources made available when required, rather than being pre-allocated.

on-premises.definition: Software or infrastructure that is located within the physical confines of an organization, as opposed to being hosted remotely.

online.definition: Connected to or available via a network, typically the internet.

open source.definition: Here "open source" is as adjective that describes software. However, it can also be a verb or a noun.

operation.definition: a task or activity performed to achieve a certain result. It involves executing a series of steps to perform a particular function.

operator.definition: A keyword beginning with a $ used to express an update, complex query, or data transformation. For example, $gt is the query language's "greater than" operator.

optional.definition: Not required; left to personal or system discretion.

organization.definition: Logical grouping of Atlas projects. You can leverage an organization to manage billing, users, and security settings for the projects it contains.

organization ID.definition: Unique 24-digit hexadecimal string used to identify your Atlas organization. The Return All Organizations endpoint returns the ID of all organizations that the authenticated user executing the API call can access.

orphaned cursor.definition: A cursor that is not properly closed or iterated over in your application code. Orphaned cursors can cause performance issues in your MongoDB deployment.

orphaned document.definition: In a sharded cluster, orphaned documents are those documents on a shard that also exist in chunks on other shards as a result of failed migrations or incomplete migration cleanup due to abnormal shutdown.

outage.definition: An outage refers to a period during which the cloud service is unavailable or not functioning as expected, leading to a disruption in service for its users.

overhead.definition: In this context as a noun, "overhead" it's a term for business expenses (such as rent, insurance, or heating) not chargeable to a particular part of the work or product.

package.definition: In the context of MongoDB Atlas, a package refers to a pre-configured set of features, tools, or services that can be easily deployed and managed on the MongoDB Atlas platform. It's important to note that the term "package" in the context of MongoDB does not typically refer to software packages or libraries in the same way it might in other software development contexts. Instead, it pertains to pre-configured setups or configurations that simplify the deployment and management of MongoDB services in the MongoDB Atlas ecosystem.

partition key.definition: a named field that you specify when you configure Atlas Device Sync whose value determines whether the user can read or write a document

partition value.definition: a value of the partition key field for a given document

partitioning.definition: A process that maps MongoDB documents in a synced MongoDB Atlas cluster into Realm objects in client realms.

partner.definition: In this context as a noun, "partner" means something like "team up" or "join"

passive member.definition: A member of a replica set that cannot become primary because its members[n].priority is 0.

passwordless.definition: An authentication mechanism that does not require a traditional password, and instead uses methods like biometrics or tokens.

pattern.definition: A recognized design or structure in MongoDB data modeling or querying that optimizes performance and scalability.

pay as you go.definition: A pricing model where users are charged based on their actual usage rather than a flat fee.

peering.definition: DNT - A VPC peering connection is a networking connection between two VPCs that enables you to route traffic between them using private IPv4 addresses or IPv6 addresses.

percentile.definition: In a dataset, a given percentile is a value where that percentage of the data falls at or below that value.

personalization.definition: The process of tailoring content or services to individual users based on their preferences or behavior.

ping.definition: A command you can use to test whether the server is responding to commands.

pipe.definition: A communication channel in UNIX-like systems allowing independent processes to send and receive data. In the UNIX shell, piped operations allow users to direct the output of one command into the input of another.

pipeline.definition: A series of operations in an aggregation process.

playback.definition: May refer to the process of replaying operations from the oplog one-by-one to recreate state at a given moment in time.

plugin.definition: a plug-in module or plug-in software.

point-in-time restore.definition: A feature that allows you to restore data to the state it was in at a given point in time.

translations.es: restauración a un punto específico del tiempo

polygon.definition: An array of LinearRing coordinate arrays

pooling.definition: The practice of sharing resources among multiple clients to maximize efficiency. In MongoDB Drivers, this may refer to a connection pool - a cache of open, ready-to-use database connections maintained by the driver.

post.definition: To perform an operation after another operation. A post processor, for example, may modify data after performing a query.

post-image document.definition: A document after it was inserted, replaced, or updated.

powerOf2Sizes.definition: A per-collection setting that changes and normalizes the way MongoDB allocates space for each document, in an effort to maximize storage reuse and to reduce fragmentation.

pre-image document.definition: A document before it was replaced, updated, or deleted.

pre-splitting.definition: An operation performed before inserting data that divides the range of possible shard key values into chunks to facilitate easy insertion and high write throughput.

prefix compression.definition: Reduces memory and disk consumption by storing any identical index key prefixes only once, per page of memory.

previous.definition: Existing or occurring before in time or order.

primary.definition: In a replica set, the primary is the member that receives all write operations. In multi-region clusters, Atlas prioritizes nodes in the Highest Priority region for primary eligibility during elections.

primary key.definition: A record's unique immutable identifier. In an RDBMS, the primary key is typically an integer stored in each row's id field. In MongoDB, the _id field holds a document's primary key which is usually a BSON ObjectId.

primary shard.definition: The shard that holds all the un-sharded collections.

priority.definition: A configurable value that helps determine which members in a replica set are most likely to become primary.

private API key.definition: A secret key used to authenticate requests to an API, ensuring that the client has permission to use the service.

private endpoints.definition: a private connection to Atlas App Services that does not go over the public internet

private key.definition: A cryptographic key that is kept secret and used for decryption or signing data.

privilege.definition: A combination of specified resource and actions permitted on the resource.

process.definition: Act of performing a series of operations on data or instructions
A series of actions or steps taken in order to achieve a particular end.

profiler.definition: The database profiler collects detailed information about Database Commands executed against a running `mongod` instance. This includes CRUD operations as well as configuration and administration commands.

project.definition: In MongoDB, this may refer to the `$project` aggregation stage, or the "project" structure that organizes resources within MongoDB.

project ID.definition: Unique 24-digit hexadecimal string used to identify your Atlas project. The Get All Projects API endpoint returns the ID of all projects that the authenticated user executing the API call can access.

project stage.definition: The `$project` aggregation stage passes along the documents with the requested fields to the next stage in the pipeline. You can use the `$project` stage to include or exclude a field, add a new field, or reset the value of an existing field.

projection.definition: A document given to a query that specifies which fields MongoDB returns in the result set.

property.definition: Logical grouping of database deployments. You can have multiple database deployments within a single project and multiple projects within a single organization.

property annotation.definition: metadata tags that you can use to customize the behavior of properties in your object models

protocol.definition: A set of rules governing the exchange or transmission of data between devices.

provisioning.definition: The process of setting up IT resources such as servers, storage, and networks.

public API key.definition: A non-secret key used to identify a client when calling a public API.

public cloud.definition: public clouds use shared infrastructure (vs private clouds that use an organization’s own infrastructure).

public key.definition: a cryptographic key that can be shared openly and is used to encrypt data or verify digital signatures, while its corresponding private key is kept secret.

query.definition: A read request. MongoDB uses a JSON-like query language that includes a variety of query operators with names that begin with a $ character.

query filter.definition: A criterion or condition used to retrieve specific data from a database.

query framework.definition: A combination of the query optimizer and query execution engine used to process an operation.

query language.definition: "query language" refers to any computer programming language that requests and retrieves data from database and information systems

query operator.definition: A keyword beginning with $ in a query.

query optimizer.definition: A process that generates query plans. For each query, the optimizer generates a plan that matches the query to the index that will return results as efficiently as possible. The optimizer reuses the query plan each time the query runs.

query plan.definition: A set of steps used by a database management system to execute a query.

query shape.definition: A combination of query predicate, sort, projection, and collation. The query shape allows MongoDB to identify logically equivalent queries and analyze their performance.

query string.definition: a part of a URL that contains parameters and values used to pass data to web applications or databases.

queryable backup.definition: A read-only snapshot of a backup from which data can be queried without needing to restore it first.

queryable fields.definition: When you configure Flexible Sync, you specify field names that your client application can query in a Flexible Sync subscription - these are queryable fields.

race condition.definition: An undesirable situation that occurs when a device or system attempts to perform two or more operations at the same time

range.definition: A contiguous range of shard key values within a chunk. Data ranges include the lower boundary and exclude the upper boundary. MongoDB migrates data when a shard contains too much data of a collection relative to other shards.

ranged.definition: Data or operations oriented around a range or interval. You can use a range in a query to find results that are within a given numeric, date, objectId, or letter (from the English alphabet) range. You can use the `$range` aggregation operator to generate a sequence of numbers incrementing by the specified step value from the start point, up to but not including the end point. You can use range as a sharding strategy to divide data into ranges based on the shard key values.

read concern.definition: Specifies a level of isolation for read operations.

read lock.definition: A shared lock on a resource such as a collection or database that, while held, allows concurrent readers but no writers.

read preference.definition: A setting that determines how clients direct read operations. Read preference affects all replica sets, including shard replica sets.

read uncommitted.definition: The lowest level of isolation in transaction processing

read-only node.definition: Replica set in a dedicated geographic region that supplements your electable node regions. You can use read-only nodes to localize data where it is most frequently read to improve performance.

real-time.definition: The immediate processing and feedback of data as events occur.

real-time data.definition: Data that is delivered immediately after collection without delay.

Realm CLI.definition: A command line interface named realm-cli from which you can manage any App.

Realm client.definition: an application on a device that uses Atlas Device SDK

Realm file.definition: the file format that the database uses to store Atlas Device SDK data on a device

Realm instance.definition: an instance of the Atlas Device SDK database on a device

Realm object.definition: An instance of a Realm object type. An object that you can store in a realm and sync with a synced MongoDB Atlas cluster.

Realm Object Model.definition: The structure that defines the fields of and relationships between all Realm objects that you can read or write into a client-local realm instance. Defined natively in the code of your client application.

Realm object type.definition: A declaration of an object structure that can be stored and synchronized using Realm. This includes primitive fields, embedded lists, and object relations. Collectively referred to as the Realm data model.

Realm Schema.definition: The structure that defines the fields of and relationships between all MongoDB documents that you can read or write into a App's linked MongoDB Atlas cluster.

Realm UI.definition: A web interface from which you can manage any App.

record.definition: In MongoDB, a record is a document, which is a data structure composed of field and value pairs.

recovering.definition: A replica set member status indicating that a member is not ready to begin normal activities of a secondary or primary. Recovering members are unavailable for reads.

recovery time objective.definition: The maximum acceptable amount of time to restore an application, system, or process after a failure or outage.

redaction.definition: The process of censoring or limiting access to the contents of log or documents fields.

region.definition: A geographically defined area where cloud services are located.

relational database.definition: A database that organizes data into tables of related data using rows and columns.

relationship.definition: A relationship is a connection between two documents.

relaxed mode.definition: A configuration setting that allows for less frequent or strict consistency checks to improve performance.

release notes.definition: refers to the technical documentation produced and distributed alongside the launch of a new software product or a product update

relevance-based search.definition: Group of MongoDB servers that maintain the same data set. Replica sets provide redundancy, high availability, and are the basis for all production deployments.

remove.definition: The length of time between the last operation in the primary's oplog and the last operation applied to a particular secondary.

render.definition: A search method that ranks results based on their relevance to the search query.

replica.definition: The process of converting website code into a visual display that users can interact with.

replica pairs.definition: refers to an exact copy or model of something

write conflict.definition: A situation in which two concurrent operations, at least one of which is a write, attempt to use a resource in a way that would violate constraints imposed by a storage engine using optimistic concurrency control. MongoDB will transparently abort and retry one of the conflicting operations.

write lock.definition: An exclusive lock on a resource such as a collection or database. When a process writes to a resource, it takes an exclusive write lock to prevent other processes from writing to or reading from that resource.

write transaction.definition: You can only write to a realm during a write transaction. Beginning or committing a write transaction has the side effect of advancing the realm version of the enclosing realm instance.

writeBacks.definition: The process within the sharding system that ensures that writes issued to a shard that is not responsible for the relevant chunk get applied to the proper shard.

zero-copy.definition: a database design strategy where object accessors point directly into database storage using memory mapping, so there is no distinction between the objects in Realm and the results of your query in application memory

zone.definition: A grouping of documents based on ranges of shard key values for a given sharded collection. Each shard in the sharded cluster can associate with one or more zones. In a balanced cluster, MongoDB directs reads and writes covered by a zone only to those shards inside the zone. See the Zones manual page for more information.
